title: Special sequences
examples: How do I find the next number in this pattern?
What is the rule for triangular numbers?
Can you show me an example of a cube number?

explain.say: Today we look at special number patterns. These are called special sequences. We will learn about squares and cubes.
A square number is found by multiplying a whole number by itself. For example, three squared is three times three, which equals nine.
A cube number is found by multiplying a whole number by itself three times. Five cubed is five times five times five, which equals one hundred twenty five.
Triangular numbers are sums of consecutive whole numbers. The third triangular number is one plus two plus three, which equals six.
The Fibonacci sequence starts with zero and one. Each number after that is the sum of the two numbers before it. The next number is one plus one, which is two.

faq.q: What is the difference between a square and a cube?
faq.a: A square number uses two factors multiplied together. A cube number uses three factors multiplied together.
asks: How many times do I multiply for a cube?
Is it always two numbers for a square?

faq.q: How do I find the next triangular number?
faq.a: You add the next whole number to the last triangular number you found. For example, after ten, you add four to get fourteen.
asks: What is the rule for triangular numbers?
Do I just add numbers together?

faq.q: Does the Fibonacci sequence always start with one and one?
faq.a: It can start with different numbers, but the most common start is zero and one. You always add the previous two terms together.
asks: What are the first few Fibonacci numbers?
How do I continue the Fibonacci sequence?

faq.q: Are all these sequences related to geometry?
faq.a: Squares and cubes relate to 2D and 3D shapes. Triangular numbers relate to stacking dots in a triangle.
asks: Can I see a picture of a square number?
Does this pattern come from shapes?

faq.q: If I know the fourth term, how do I find the fifth?
faq.a: You must know the rule for that specific sequence. For Fibonacci, you add the third and fourth terms together.

facts: The sequence of square numbers is $n^2$: 1, 4, 9, 16, 25...
The sequence of cube numbers is $n^3$: 1, 8, 27, 64, 125...
Triangular numbers are the sum of all whole numbers up to a certain number.
In the Fibonacci sequence, each number is the sum of the two preceding ones.

quiz.say: What is the fifth square number?
quiz.why: You multiply five by five to get twenty five.

wrong.0: This mistake happens if you multiply five by five and then by ten.
wrong.1: This is incorrect because you might only multiply five by four.
wrong.3: This is a common mistake because you might add five and five.

quiz.why: You add the last two numbers, three and five, to get eight.

wrong.0: This is incorrect because you only added the last number and the one before it.
wrong.1: This mistake happens if you add the two numbers before the last one.
wrong.3: This mistake happens if you add three times two plus four.

quiz.why: You add the next whole number, which is five, to the last term ten.

wrong.0: This mistake happens if you only add two to the last number.
wrong.1: This is incorrect because you might be thinking of square numbers.
wrong.2: This mistake happens if you add the next two whole numbers.
